transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Well, honestly, what made me come in is I feel like the warm part of me just... shut off. I sit with my husband, or I try to watch my shows after work, and I know I should feel some comfort or even a little happy, but... there’s just nothing there right now.
When did you first notice this feeling of numbness or lack of warmth start? Was it sudden, or did it develop gradually over time?

It was pretty sudden. Um, it's been going on for about three weeks now. It started right after... well, ever since a pallet collapsed at work and injured my coworker. I've just felt this way since that happened.
Since the pallet collapse, have you been having unwanted thoughts or images about that incident that keep coming back to you, even when you don't want them to?

Yeah, I have. It's... out of nowhere, I'll just see that pallet coming down again, or I'll hear the crash in my head. It's especially bad at work. Like, if a forklift beeps or somebody drops something in the warehouse, it just flashes right back, and my stomach just turns.
Since the pallet collapse, have you been trying to avoid going to work, or staying away from certain areas of the warehouse, or avoiding things that remind you of what happened?

No, I haven't really done that. I mean, I still go to work every day, and I haven't tried to stay away from any particular aisles or anything. I just do my job. It's not like I'm trying to avoid the warehouse or the pallets. I just... I just have those thoughts pop up, but I haven't changed my routine or stayed away from anything.
When you have these flashbacks or intrusive thoughts about the pallet collapse, how much distress do they cause you? And has this been affecting your ability to concentrate at work or do your job?

Well, they cause a lot of distress, honestly. It's really messed up my ability to do my job. I'm actually not even able to do my regular receiving work right now. Um, the other day I completely froze up during a pallet move, and then I ended up snapping at one of my coworkers. After that, my supervisor had to take me off the floor. They said I just wasn't functioning safely out there. So, yeah, it's definitely affecting my work.

You mentioned these symptoms started about three weeks ago after the pallet collapse. Do you expect these feelings and flashbacks to go away soon, or do you think they might continue for a while longer?

I don't really know, honestly. I mean, I hope they go away soon, but... it's been three weeks and it hasn't really gotten any better. If anything, it feels like it's harder to deal with now because it's affecting my job so much. I just don't know how long it's going to last.
When you describe that warm part of you shutting off, do you ever feel like you're watching yourself from outside your body, or like things around you don't feel real—like you're in a fog or a dream?

No, I wouldn't say that. I don't feel like I'm outside my body or anything weird like that. And things around me feel real enough... it's not like a dream. It's just more like I'm emotionally blank, you know? But I'm definitely still in my own body, and I know where I am.

You mentioned these symptoms started about three weeks ago. Just to clarify the timeline—do you think these feelings and flashbacks will likely be gone within the next week or two, or are you expecting them to stick around for at least another few weeks or longer?

I mean, I really can't say for sure. Like I said before, I hope they go away, but... I just don't know. I don't really have a timeline in my head for when this is going to stop. I'm just kind of taking it day by day right now.

Based on how you're feeling now, do you think it's realistic that these symptoms—the flashbacks, the emotional numbness, the difficulty at work—could be mostly resolved within the next couple of months, or does it feel like this might be something you're dealing with for a longer period than that?

I really don't know. Um, I mean, I can't predict the future. It feels pretty heavy right now, so it's hard to imagine it just being gone in a couple of months, but... I don't know if it's going to last longer than that either. I'm just trying to get through my shifts at work right now without losing it. I haven't really thought that far ahead.

When you think about these symptoms you're experiencing now—the flashbacks, the emotional numbness, the trouble at work—do you think it's more likely they'll be mostly gone within the next month, or do you think they'll still be significantly affecting you after a month has passed?

Honestly, like I was just saying... I really just don't know. I feel like we keep coming back to this, but I can't give you a timeline. I hope it's all gone in a month, but I have no idea if it actually will be. I'm really just trying to make it through my shifts right now without falling apart. I just don't know what to expect.

I know you're uncertain about the exact timeline, but let me ask it this way: do you think it's more likely than not that you'll still be having these flashbacks and emotional numbness a month from now, or do you think they're more likely to be mostly gone by then?

I really... I just don't know how to answer that. I get that you're trying to figure out how long this will last, but I honestly have no clue. I'm not trying to be difficult, I just... I don't know if it's more likely or less likely. I'm just trying to get through today.
If you're still having these flashbacks and feeling emotionally numb a month from now, would that surprise you, or does that feel like something that could realistically happen?

I guess... no, it wouldn't surprise me. The way things are right now, with how intense it all feels, it seems like a real possibility that I'll still be dealing with it in a month. I don't want that to be the case, obviously, but it wouldn't shock me if it is.
If you're still having these flashbacks and feeling emotionally numb three months from now, would that surprise you, or does that feel like it could realistically happen?

I mean... three months? That's a long time. I honestly don't know. I guess I'd be a little surprised if it was still exactly this bad after three whole months, but... I don't know. Like I said, I'm just trying to get through right now. Thinking about three months from now is just too much.

Let me ask this more directly: do you think it's more likely that these symptoms will still be significantly bothering you after one month passes, or more likely that they'll be mostly better by then?

I... I really can't say for sure. I mean, I want to say they'll be better by then, but with how bad it is right now, it feels like it's more likely they'll still be bothering me. I just... I don't know for certain. I'm just guessing.

Just to be completely clear about the timing: the pallet collapse happened, and then within the first few days after that, these flashbacks and emotional numbness started showing up—is that right, or did they start a bit later, like after a week or so had passed?

Yeah, it was pretty much right away, within those first few days. It didn't take a week to start. Um, all of this has been going on for about three weeks now, basically ever since the pallet collapsed and injured my coworker.
When you imagine yourself one month from now, do you think you'll still be having these flashbacks and feeling emotionally numb, or do you expect them to be gone by then?

Um, I think I just answered that... I really don't know. Like I said a minute ago, I'd like to expect them to be gone, but I just can't say for sure. I really don't know what it'll be like a month from now.

If I told you that in one month from today you'd still be having these same flashbacks and feeling emotionally numb like you do right now, would you say that's unlikely to happen, or would you say that's actually what you expect?

I... I don't mean to be difficult, but I really don't know how else to answer that. I just don't know what to expect. I'm hoping it's unlikely, but with how things are right now, I just can't predict how I'll be in a month.

Let me ask it differently: thinking about when the pallet collapse happened three weeks ago as the starting point, do you think these flashbacks and numbness will still be present after a full month has passed from that day—so roughly about a week from now?

I mean... I honestly don't know. A week from now? It's hard to say. I'd like to think things will settle down by then, but since it's been going on for three weeks already, I just really can't tell you if it'll be gone or not. I'm just taking it day by day right now.

Let me ask you this way: do you think it's more likely that a month from now you'll still be having these flashbacks and emotional numbness, or more likely that they'll be mostly gone by then? I need you to pick one.

Look, I know you need me to pick one, but I... I really just can't. I'm not trying to be stubborn about this. I honestly just don't have an answer for you. I don't know which is more likely. I mean, obviously I want them to be gone, but sitting here right now, I just don't know what's going to happen. I just can't predict it for you.

She meets criteria for ASD: (1) exposure to a traumatic event; (2) intrusive symptoms (flashbacks, unwanted images triggered by sensory cues); (3) emotional numbing/detachment; (4) functional impairment (unable to perform work duties, froze during pallet move, snapped at coworker); (5) symptom onset within days of trauma (3 weeks duration total); (6) no avoidance behaviors or dissociative symptoms (depersonalization/derealization). F43.10 (without prolonged exposure) is more appropriate than F43.11 (with prolonged exposure) given the patient explicitly denies avoidance behaviors.
